free_tier.stated: none: gigarapid.com is a GoDaddy for-sale page - 'GigaRapid.com is for sale! ... Own it today for $2,695, or select Lease to Own.' The EUR 0.99 Eco plan that price indexes still list is not purchasable.

record.interface_detail: no interface: the domain is listed for sale
record.chaining: removed from the candidate set; the cheapest plan any index reports for this name cannot be bought
record.binding_note: no constraint applies to a parked for-sale domain

identity_cost.detail: not applicable; nothing can be registered

record.reliability_note: The domain is parked for sale, so any price index that still lists a EUR 0.99 plan is stale and would send a buyer to a dead checkout
record.confidence_note: Measured by probe on 2026-10-23: https://gigarapid.com/ returned 200 and redirected to forsale.godaddy.com with the text 'GigaRapid.com is for sale!' and the price USD 2,695 (lease USD 450/month). Two price indexes still quote GigaRapid Eco AF10 at EUR 0.99, which is how a stale index costs a session.

evidence.proved: redirect to forsale.godaddy.com; page text 'GigaRapid.com is for sale! ... Own it today for $2,695, or select Lease to Own ... USD$450 / month'
third-party index still lists 'GigaRapid Eco AF10 at EUR 0.99 per month' as the cheapest plan, which the parked domain disproves

record.notes: This is the clearest case in the sector of a price index outliving its provider. The index is useful for breadth and must never be the evidence for a number; the parked page is the evidence here.

extras.death_evidence: GoDaddy for-sale landing page at USD 2,695
